subtitle: Master the technique of tonicizing other keys temporarily for harmonic interest

backLink.label: Back to Chord Theory in Songs

introduction.title: Temporary Key Changes
introduction.text: Secondary dominants are like taking brief vacations to other keys without actually leaving home. By treating any chord as if it were a temporary tonic, you can create stronger resolutions and more sophisticated harmonic motion.

columns.title: Stronger Resolutions
columns.text: V7 → I is the strongest progression in music. Secondary dominants let you use this power anywhere.

columns.title: Chromatic Color
columns.text: Adds chromatic notes that aren't in the key, creating sophisticated harmonic colors.

cards.title: The Basic Principle
cards.description: Any chord can be preceded by its own dominant. In the key of C major:
items: Dm can be preceded by A7 (the V7 of D minor)
F can be preceded by C7 (the V7 of F major)
Am can be preceded by E7 (the V7 of A minor)

cards.title: V/ii (A7)

fields.label: Analysis
fields.value: A7 contains C# which leads strongly to D

fields.label: Usage
fields.value: Very common - tonicizes the ii chord

items: "Autumn Leaves"
Many folk songs

cards.title: V/iii (B7)

fields.label: Analysis
fields.value: B7 contains D# which leads to E

fields.label: Usage
fields.value: Less common but effective for minor flavor

items: "My Funny Valentine"
Jazz ballads

cards.title: V/IV (C7)

fields.label: Analysis
fields.value: C7 contains Bb which leads to F

items: "Sweet Caroline"
Country standards

cards.title: V/V (D7)

fields.label: Analysis
fields.value: D7 contains F# which leads to G

items: "I Got Rhythm"
Thousands of songs

cards.title: V/vi (E7)

fields.label: Analysis
fields.value: E7 contains G# which leads to A

items: "House of the Rising Sun"
"California Dreamin'"

cards.title: Circle of Fifths with Secondary Dominants

fields.label: Without secondary dominants
fields.value: C - F - Bb - Eb - Ab - Db - Gb - B - E - A - D - G - C

fields.label: With secondary dominants
fields.value: C - C7 - F - F7 - Bb - Bb7 - Eb...

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Each major chord becomes a dominant 7th leading to the next chord down a 5th

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: E7 strongly tonicizes Am, making it feel temporarily like a tonic

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: D7 prepares G7 more strongly than simple ii7-V7 motion

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: C7 makes the move to F feel like a strong resolution

cards.title: Leading Tone Creation
cards.description: Secondary dominants create leading tones to non-tonic chords

fields.label: Example
fields.value: In C major, D7 (V/V) creates F# which leads to G

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Any time you want to strongly emphasize a target chord

cards.title: Temporary Tonicization
cards.description: The target chord temporarily feels like a new tonic

fields.label: Example
fields.value: E7 → Am makes Am feel like "home" momentarily

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Creating key centers within a progression

cards.title: Chromatic Voice Leading
cards.description: Secondary dominants often create chromatic bass lines

fields.label: Example
fields.value: C - C7 - F creates bass line C - C - F with chromatic harmony

cards.title: Circle of Fifths Motion
cards.description: Chain secondary dominants for continuous forward motion

fields.label: Example
fields.value: A7 - D7 - G7 - C (V/ii - V/V - V - I)

cards.title: Secondary Dominants in Popular Music

fields.label: Analysis
fields.value: I - V/IV - IV - V - I (in C major)

items: C7 contains Bb (not in C major)
Bb strongly wants to resolve down to A
But it resolves to F instead, creating satisfaction
Makes F feel like a temporary "home"

cards.title: Why It's Effective
items: Simple but sophisticated harmonic motion
Creates forward momentum to the IV chord
Adds just enough sophistication without complexity
Perfect for sing-along accessibility
Emotional Effect: Confident → Slightly uncertain → Resolved satisfaction

cards.title: Popular Music Patterns
items: I - V/vi - vi - IV: C - E7 - Am - F (Makes vi feel like temporary tonic)
I - V/IV - IV - V: C - C7 - F - G (Country/folk progression)
vi - V/V - V - I: Am - D7 - G - C (Strong cadential motion)

cards.title: Jazz/Advanced Patterns
items: ii - V/V - V - I: Dm - D7 - G - C (Enhanced ii-V-I progression)
V/ii - ii - V - I: A7 - Dm - G - C (Extended ii-V-I approach)
Circle of Fifths: A7-D7-G7-C (Chain of secondary dominants)

exercises.title: Step-by-Step Practice
items: 1. Learn all V7 chords in every key
2. Practice V7 → I resolutions
3. Insert secondary dominants into simple progressions
4. Practice circle of fifths with dominants
5. Analyze songs you know for secondary dominants

exercises.title: Listening Practice
items: Notice when a chord sounds "outside" the key
Feel the extra tension before resolution
Identify the chromatic notes being added
Listen for temporary key center shifts
Study jazz standards for advanced usage
